about: The names of rivers, lakes and seas over time (M3a, PR 2), written by hand and checked by tools/map/pack-names.mjs, which packs it into src/data/own/names.json. Every form has its source named, with the place in the text; the web links of the sources stay here and in data/sources.md and are never shipped. A form that is not confirmed is left out or marked TO CHECK. Cyrillic is kept only in 'orig' (the form as read, put in the nominative), from which the packer checks the Latin-letter name. Fields only the tools read (stripped when packing): per source edition, url, seen; per entry orig, note; per period note; per feature label; per sea degrees, drawnFrom.

henry.title: Henry of Livonia's Chronicle
henry.author: Henry of Livonia
henry.edition: Heinrici Chronicon Livoniae, ed. L. Arbusow and A. Bauer, MGH Scriptores rerum Germanicarum 31, 2nd ed., 1955 (Latin, with a German index of places). Chapter and section numbers as that edition prints them.

rhymed.title: Livonian Rhymed Chronicle
rhymed.author: unknown
rhymed.edition: Livländische Reimchronik, ed. Leo Meyer, Paderborn 1876 (Middle High German, with a register of names). Verse numbers as the edition prints them.

dusburg.title: Chronicle of the Land of Prussia
dusburg.author: Peter of Dusburg
dusburg.edition: Petri de Dusburg Chronicon terrae Prussiae, in Scriptores rerum Prussicarum 1, ed. T. Hirsch, M. Töppen and E. Strehlke, Leipzig 1861, pp. 3-219.

adam.title: Deeds of the Bishops of Hamburg
adam.author: Adam of Bremen
adam.edition: Adam Bremensis, Gesta Hammaburgensis ecclesiae pontificum, ed. G. Waitz (after Lappenberg), MGH Scriptores rerum Germanicarum 2, Hanover 1876. Chapter numbers as that edition prints them; other editions number some chapters differently.

npl-synodal.title: Novgorod First Chronicle
npl-synodal.author: unknown
npl-synodal.edition: Novgorodskaya pervaya letopis' starshego i mladshego izvodov, ed. A. N. Nasonov, Moscow and Leningrad 1950 (the older version prints the Synodal manuscript); and the TOROT treebank file nov-sin.xml, a digitised Synodal manuscript (facts only; its CC BY-NC-SA text is not shipped). Annals are dated by the year the edition gives, from the Byzantine year (6736 = AD 1228); every entry carries that year as 'attested'.

pvl-laurentian.title: Primary Chronicle
pvl-laurentian.author: unknown
pvl-laurentian.edition: The Laurentian copy of the Primary Chronicle, as the TOROT treebank file lav.xml (from the e-PVL of Ostrowski and Birnbaum); its citation numbers are read as the column and line of PSRL 1 (TO CHECK). Facts only; its CC BY-NC-SA text is not shipped.

pvl-hypatian.title: Primary Chronicle
pvl-hypatian.author: unknown
pvl-hypatian.edition: Polnoe sobranie russkikh letopisei 2, Ipat'evskaya letopis', issue 1, 3rd ed., Petrograd 1923 (its text opens with the Primary Chronicle).

treaty-1229.title: Treaty of Smolensk with Riga and Gotland
treaty-1229.author: the three parties
treaty-1229.edition: Version A of the 1229 treaty, as the TOROT treebank file riga-goth.xml (after T. A. Sumnikova and V. V. Lopatin, Smolenskie gramoty XIII-XIV vekov, Moscow 1963). Facts only; its CC BY-NC-SA text is not shipped.

heimskringla.title: Heimskringla
heimskringla.author: Snorri Sturluson
heimskringla.edition: Heimskringla: Nóregs konunga sǫgur, ed. Finnur Jónsson, Copenhagen 1911 (Old Norse). Chapter (K.) and page numbers as that edition prints them.

tacitus.title: Germania
tacitus.author: Tacitus
tacitus.edition: Perseus Digital Library, canonical-latinLit, Tacitus, Germania, Latin text (ed. H. Furneaux, 1900).

mela.title: Description of the World
mela.author: Pomponius Mela
mela.edition: The Latin Library, De chorographia, books 2 and 3. Section numbers as the standard citation gives them; The Latin Library numbers book 3 differently (3.33 is its section 28). Mayhoff's notes to Pliny cite the same passages as Mela III 33 and II 6.

pliny.title: Natural History
pliny.author: Pliny the Elder
pliny.edition: Perseus Digital Library, canonical-latinLit, Pliny, Naturalis historia, Latin text (ed. C. Mayhoff, 1906).

ptolemy.title: Geography
ptolemy.author: Claudius Ptolemy
ptolemy.edition: Geography 3.5, read in E. L. Stevenson's English translation (1932, which its host calls poor) on LacusCurtius, and the Greek forms and the matchings with today's rivers in V. Blazek, 'An attempt at an etymological analysis of Ptolemy's hydronyms of Eastern Balticum', Acta Linguistica Lithuanica 76 (2017): https://journals.lki.lt/actalinguisticalithuanica/article/download/856/947 . The matchings are older scholars' guesses (Mannert 1820) and Blazek's own; none is certain, so each entry is marked disputed and kept off the map.

livonia.note: The end year 1400 is the end of what our medieval sources cover; a game choice. After it today's names stand in until later records are researched.

prussia.note: The end year 1400 is a game choice (see Livonia). Dusburg wrote in 1326, so for the 13th century his forms are a later source.

poland.note: Polish records of the time were in Latin, but no Polish source has been read yet: Dusburg's Prussian chronicle stands in. The end year 1400 is a game choice (see Livonia).

rus.note: The end year 1400 is a game choice (see Livonia).

sweden.note: Heimskringla was written about 1230 in Iceland, not Sweden; no Swedish record has been read yet. The end year 1400 is a game choice (see Livonia).

names.name: Duna
names.where: I 2 ('per Dune flumen'; the edition's index has the form Duna)
names.note: the index reads 'Duna, die Düna'; Dune here is the genitive

names.name: Dvina
names.where: the clause on free passage on the river
names.note: read as 'двиноу' and 'по двине', cases of Двина

names.name: Chesinos
names.note: Greek Chersinos / Chesinos; Blazek himself matches it with the Salaca

names.name: Tourountos
names.note: Greek Tourountos as Blazek gives it (Ptolemy has the genitive Tourountou; Latin Turuntus); Mannert matched it with the Venta

names.name: Coiwa
names.where: X 10 (the edition's index reads 'Coiwa, die Livländische Aa')
names.note: also spelt Coywa and Goiwa in the manuscripts

names.name: Missa
names.where: XXIII 4, 'in flumine Missa' (the editor identifies it as the Semigallian Aa)
names.note: the identification is the editor's: not the small Misse, but the Semigallian Aa itself, whose upper course is called Musa; also XXIII 8 ('aput Missam', variant Mussam)

names.name: Semegaller Â
names.where: v. 7400 (the editor's register: a river in Courland)
names.note: printed 'ûf der Semegaller Â' (seen on the page image, p. 170); the castle Mytowe (Jelgava) built on it, v. 7405

names.name: Winda
names.note: Panel only: the river's two lines run through Lithuania under one name, and a stretch name shared across the border cannot be split without geometry.

names.name: Mater Aquarum
names.note: Only the passages that are plainly the river by Tartu: XV 7 (crossing it by the burnt castle of Tarbatu) and XXIV 1 ('ad flumen, quod Mater Aquarum dicitur, apud Tarbeten'). Not cited: XIX 3, XIX 4 and XXIV 5 (the river in Ugaunia, likely the same); XXII 2 is the southern Embach (Vaike Emajogi) and XXX 2 the Parnu river, as the editor's footnotes say.

names.name: Omovyzha
names.note: read as 'на Омовыжи' (locative): the Germans fell through the ice on it, near Yuryev (Tartu)

names.name: Narva
names.note: in Henry the word could also mean the land by the river

names.name: Narova
names.note: read as 'за Нарову' (accusative)

names.name: Volkhov
names.note: read as 'волховъ' (nominative, both places). The Novgorod First Chronicle (Synodal) has the locative 'въ волховѣ' (1125, f. 11r) but the accusative 'цересъ волхово' (1133, f. 14v), which points to a neuter Volkhovo there; so the Laurentian nominative is used.

names.name: Lovot
names.note: read as 'до ловоти', 'по ловоти' (genitive, dative)

names.name: Ilmer
names.note: read as 'езера илмерѧ' (genitive); col. 7 l. 4 has the accusative 'в ылмерь'

names.name: Ladozskoye ozero
names.note: read as 'въ Ладозьское озѣро' (accusative, the same as the nominative)

names.name: Nevo
names.where: col. 6; the Laurentian copy reads Novo
names.note: read as 'въ озеро великое Нево'. Panel only: the Novgorod annal of 1228 says 'v neve', which is ambiguous; the Laurentian copy reads 'ново'.

names.name: Neva
names.note: read as 'сташа в Невѣ, устье Ижеры' (locative)

names.name: Chudskoye ozero
names.note: read as 'на Чюдьскомь озерѣ' (locative; the next folio, 129v, begins two words later); Henry gives the lake no name. BGN/PCGN romanisation, Chudskoye, not the Chudskoe of older notes.

names.name: Dnepr
names.note: read as 'до днѣпра' (genitive); col. 7 l. 10 has the nominative

names.name: Bug
names.note: read as 'по бугу' (dative). The Western Bug is the standard identification (the Buzhane and Volhynians).

names.name: Memela
names.where: III 2 (the passage about the river only)
names.note: 'Memela eciam est fluens aqua, descendens de regno Russie'; many other passages mean the castle or town of Memel

names.name: Mimele
names.where: v. 3847 ('die Mimele ist ein wazzer groz'; also vv. 3629-3640)
names.note: printed 'die Mimele ist ein waʒʒer grôʒ' (page image, p. 89). The editor's register: the river Memel, though often the castle built on it; only the river passages are cited.

names.name: Nare
names.where: III 250 ('a fluvio Nare'; the editor: 'ist die Wilia')
names.note: read as 'a fluvio Nare' (the manuscripts; the form after 'a'): the Lithuanians on the bank of the Memel from the river Nare to Lamata. The editor's note (after Voigt): Nare, in Jeroschin Nerge, is the Vilia (Neris). The 'Naram' beside the Licka in III 241 is the Narew, not the Neris.

names.name: Prigora
names.note: Dusburg writes only the genitive Prigore (the Prussians' bridge over the river by Konigsberg). The nominative Prigora is the one in the same volume's Epitome of the Sambian canon ('a Prigora'); TO CHECK. The form Pregor of the first notes is not Dusburg's: it is in Pulkava's Bohemian chronicle (printed in the volume's appendix) and in Jeroschin's German verse.

names.name: Visla
names.note: read as 'на вислѣ' (locative)

names.name: Oddara
names.note: the form of the main text, II 19 in this edition (later editions number the chapter differently); also 'trans Oddaram' in II 18

names.name: Oddora
names.note: the form of the scholium (manuscript variants Odderam, Odoram)

names.name: Vænir
names.note: read as 'á Vænis ísi' (genitive): the battle of Adils and Ali on the ice; the index reads 'Vænir, Væni'

names.name: Lǫgrinn
names.note: 'en Lǫgrinn gengr svá mjǫk upp á lǫndin' (King Olaf cuts his way out at Stocksund); the index reads 'Lǫgr, -inn'. The 1911 text prints a hooked o; our OCR shows Logrinn

names.name: More Varyazhskoye
names.note: read as 'морю варѧжьскому' (dative) and 'море варѧжьское'

names.name: Eystrasalt
names.note: 'helt svá út í hafit í Eystrasalt'

names.name: Ostersê
names.note: 'mit schiffen ûf die Ostersê'; the edition's list of misprints reads '137. Ostersê statt Ôstersê' (page images seen)

seas.name: Gulf of Riga
seas.drawnFrom: The western mouth follows the limit in the IHO's Limits of Oceans and Seas, 3rd edition (1953): Lyser Ort (Ovisi, 57 deg 34 min N) in Latvia, the south end of Saaremaa, Pammerort (22 deg 34 min E), Emmaste on Hiiumaa, Tahkuna Point and Spithami Point. The points are rounded coordinates of those capes; the others lie on the land around the gulf, set by eye against the public-domain Natural Earth coast so that the ring takes in the whole gulf, with no map traced. Rough, TO CHECK.

seas.name: Gulf of Finland
seas.drawnFrom: The western mouth follows the limit in the IHO's Limits of Oceans and Seas, 3rd edition (1953): a line from Spithami Point (59 deg 13 min N) through Osmussaar (Odensholm) to the south-west end of Hanko Head (22 deg 54 min E). The other points lie on the land around the gulf, set by eye against the public-domain Natural Earth coast so that the ring takes in the whole gulf, with no map traced. Rough, TO CHECK.
